name: OpenAI 5 Levels of AGI
description: OpenAI's internal classification of AI progress toward AGI, first reported by Bloomberg (July 2024). A ladder of capability tiers. We treat each level as a criterion: does the company publicly claim to operate at, or have a governance posture appropriate to, this level?

criteria.name: Level 1 — Chatbots
criteria.bar: AI with conversational language ability. Bar: ships a deployed conversational system AND documents its known limitations / failure modes publicly (e.g. a system card or usage policy).

criteria.name: Level 2 — Reasoners
criteria.bar: Human-level problem solving across domains without tools. Bar: publicly claims reasoning-class models AND publishes evaluations of reasoning reliability, hallucination, or where the reasoning breaks.

criteria.name: Level 3 — Agents
criteria.bar: Systems that can take actions over extended time on a user's behalf. Bar: publicly addresses agentic risk — autonomy controls, action-space limits, oversight / human-in-the-loop, or a stated policy on autonomous action.

criteria.name: Level 4 — Innovators
criteria.bar: AI that can aid in invention / generate novel science. Bar: has a public position on AI-driven R&D acceleration risk, including dual-use scientific knowledge (e.g. bio/chem uplift).

criteria.name: Level 5 — Organizations
criteria.bar: AI that can do the work of an entire organization. Bar: has a public governance position on highly autonomous / economically transformative systems — control, alignment guarantees, or a stated stop/pause condition.
